thought.text: The build assets are present and PHP works. Let me do a definitive end-to-end login test: I'll temporarily set a known password on a local demo user (id=1, R1), log in, confirm authenticated access, then restore the original password.

reasoning_content:
Everything is working:
1. ✅ ddev installed and project started
2. ✅ openldap container running with all 10 test users loaded
3. ✅ composer install complete
4. ✅ npm i complete
5. ✅ DB dump imported (9 tables)
6. ✅ web.config.local.php created
7. ✅ Web app responds: `/` → 302 to /login, /login → 200 with rendered HTML
8. ✅ PHP + DB working (login form POST executed DB query, generated session)
9. ✅ Build assets present in public/theme

Let me do a definitive end-to-end login test with a real user. I'll temporarily set a known password on the DB demo user and log in to prove the entire auth stack works. This is the strongest verification of "software is installed correctly."

Let me set the password on user id=1 (R1, the top-level planner) to a known value, log in, confirm access to a dashboard page, then restore the original password.

action.command: su - dev -c 'cd /workspace && export PATH=$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH && ddev exec mysql -uroot -proot db -N -e "SELECT password FROM user WHERE id=1;" 2>/dev/null > /tmp/orig_pw.txt && echo "orig saved: $(cut -c1-15 /tmp/orig_pw.txt)..." && ddev exec mysql -uroot -proot db -e "UPDATE user SET password='\$2y\$10\$kH8s/g.D9IcpRl3P7PtUCOt3jNsv1UrYwY3GNTJe.DXyIUluaTRRC' WHERE id=1;" 2>&1 && echo "password set"'
